courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: One cleanup work I want to do is that when we have no bookings, we should probably show a short message
here.
So in our bookings page, we are relying on loaded bookings being an array with the elements in there.
Well since this all is in one ion-column, I can simply add an ngIf check on that column here, if loaded bookings
is a thing,
so if it is not undefined and then loaded bookings length is greater than zero, then I want to show this
list,
otherwise I'll add a new ion-column here with my same size and offset and then here, the ngIf check
will be if loaded bookings is not a thing, if it is undefined or if loaded
bookings length for smaller or equal to zero, then I will show this column and its content and the content
here will be a paragraph where I say no bookings found, like this. Now let me also add text center
here to center that text and if this now reloads, we should see no bookings found here.
As soon as I do add a booking however, I will simply give this a try here real quick,
if I go back to bookings, now we see that. Now this is nice,
if I remove it, we should see the text again,
we do
but the other problem I had was that we can actually book places here which are just all place but not
bookable because we have no bookable places here.
So I can certainly inspect these places but the book button shouldn't be there for these places.
Now that of course can also be fixed in a way that is similar to how we fixed it for our filter here.
So let's go to the place detail page and in there, we're fetching our place, right?
We're fetching our place data here and we're updating this whenever we get a new parameter, a new place
ID in our URL parameters and then we're loading our place here because this also gets updated
whenever our places would change and then we're loading our place here.
Now what we can do here,
again utilizing some UI state again, we can add a new property, isBookable and by default let's say
that is false but it is up to you what you set as a default
and then we inject our auth service into this page here,
so auth service is injected,
make sure to adjust your import path here.
With the auth service injected here,
now when we fetch a place and we set this place, we set this isBookable equal to a check where we
have a look at that places userId
and if that is not equal to this auth service userId, then this will return true and therefore isBookable
will be true which it should be
if IDs don't match but if IDs do match, then we are the creator of that place and therefore isBookable
will be false because I'm checking for the opposite here.
So isBookable will be false if we must not book it and hence now here in the template of
the place detail page where I render that button, we can add an ngIf statement on that entire row
here and say that this should only be bookable
if isBookable is true basically.
So isBookable is that new property I added
and only if that is true, this button should be shown
and therefore now as this reloads, if I go to this place,
I don't see that button.
Now let me simulate that I'm a different user by quickly going to the auth service and changing my
ID to XYZ instead of ABC which is the ID I added to all the dummy places.
Now this reloads and I see them here under all places and also under bookable places
and therefore if I visit such a place, I see that book button again and I can again enter my value here
and let me prolong my stay here a little bit.
So now this looks better and now I see my bookings here and I can cancel them of course.
So this is now much much better,
what's missing of course is our persistent state management where we also store this on a server and
that is what we'll focus on in the next module.
